text.en:
In a museum Dhruv saw a tall polished stone pillar with letters carved on it. A guide said, "It was put up by Emperor Ashoka more than two thousand years ago."
"What does it say?" asked Dhruv. "It tells people to be kind and to care for each other," said the guide.

Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire around 321 BCE with the help of his advisor Chanakya, also known as Kautilya. The capital was Pataliputra. The empire grew to include most of the Indian subcontinent.
Ashoka was the most famous Mauryan emperor. After the bloody Kalinga war he felt great sorrow and chose the path of non-violence and dhamma, a code of kindness and moral conduct. He had messages carved on rocks and pillars, called edicts, in the languages and scripts of the people.
The Mauryans had a strong government with officers, a large army, roads and trade. Ashoka's lion capital at Sarnath is India's national emblem.
Chandragupta Maurya started the Mauryan Empire with Chanakya's help. The capital was Pataliputra.
Ashoka felt great sorrow after the Kalinga war and chose non-violence.
He had messages of kindness carved on rocks and pillars. These are edicts.
The lion capital of Ashoka at Sarnath is our national emblem.

problem.en: Why did Ashoka have edicts carved on rocks and pillars?

text.en: He wanted to share messages with all his people.
Stones last for centuries and can be placed in public places.
So the edicts spread his ideas of kindness and dhamma.

why.en: They are also a source of history for us.

prompt.en: A friend says Ashoka was famous only for winning wars. How will you correct this?

requiredIdeas.en: After the Kalinga war he chose non-violence and dhamma.
His edicts promoted kindness and care for people and animals.

points.en: Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire; Chanakya advised him.
Ashoka chose non-violence after the Kalinga war.
His edicts are important sources of history.
